p: A safari park visit works a little differently to a walk-round zoo, so a bit of prep goes a long way. Make sure everyone has had a toilet stop before you set off on the drive, because once you're in the reserves you won't be popping out. Fill up with fuel beforehand, keep snacks and drinks within reach in the car, and give the windows a clean so the kids get a clear view. Phones and cameras with a bit of zoom will help you grab shots of the animals that keep their distance.

If you're worried about the baboons, take the advice on the route seriously. Those clever monkeys have been known to have a fiddle with wipers, aerials and anything else that isn't screwed down, and while it's hilarious to watch, it's less funny if it's your car. The park sits within the grounds of Knowsley Hall, the historic seat of the Earls of Derby, so the parkland around the reserves is attractive in its own right.

There's a lot to do nearby once you've had your fill of lions. Croxteth Hall and Country Park, on the edge of Liverpool, has a grand house, a walled garden and a working farm, plus wide grassy spaces to explore. In Liverpool itself, the Royal Albert Dock is home to the Merseyside Maritime Museum and The Beatles Story, and the Museum of Liverpool on the waterfront tells the story of the city. All of that is within half an hour or so of Prescot on a good run, so you can easily tie it into a bigger weekend.
